S39.02.note: The support text says Settings, Memory, but the real path is Settings, Personalization, Memory.
steps: Open Settings and choose Personalization.
Find the row Persistent memory with its switch.
Turn the switch off, then open a new chat and ask about a fact you saved before.
Compare: with the switch off the assistant should not use saved memories, and the switch should stay off after a reload.

S39.03.needs: a signed-in account with older chats
S39.03.note: The switch is separate from Persistent memory and is not disabled by it.
steps: Open Settings and choose Personalization.
Find the row Search past chats and its switch.
Turn it off, then in a new chat ask about something said in an older chat.
Compare: the assistant should not pull excerpts from other chats while the switch is off.

S39.04.needs: a signed-in account with saved memories
S39.04.note: The Manage memories button is disabled when no memories are saved.
steps: Open Settings and choose Personalization.
Scroll to the Memory block and click Manage memories.
Look at the list that opens below the Memory block.
Compare: every saved memory should appear in the list.

S39.05.needs: a signed-in account with several saved memories
S39.05.note: The search box only appears when at least one memory exists.
steps: Open Settings, Personalization, then click Manage memories.
Click the box that says Search memory.
Type a word that appears in one saved memory.
Compare: only the memories that contain that text should stay in the list.
S39.05.where: Settings > Personalization > Memory > Manage memories > Search memory box

S39.06.needs: a signed-in account with saved memories of different kinds
S39.06.note: The headings come from each memory's category, so a tester may see only one group if all memories share a category.
steps: Open Settings, Personalization, then click Manage memories.
Look for group headings above the memory lists.
Compare: memories should sit under headings such as Preferences, About you, Decisions, Context, Summaries, Skills, or Other.
S39.06.where: Settings > Personalization > Memory > Manage memories (group headings)

S39.09.needs: a signed-in account with memory on and ongoing chats
S39.09.note: The Work in progress section only appears when the recap has ongoing work; when memory is off Reflect shows Memory is off.
steps: Open Settings and choose Reflect.
Wait for the recap to load, then scroll down.
Look for a section titled Work in progress that lists chat titles with short descriptions.
Compare: it should list the projects or ongoing work the assistant knows about.

S39.10.note: Adding works only when the Cloud memory is ready; otherwise the page shows Cloud memory is unavailable.
steps: Open Settings, Personalization, then click Manage memories.
Click the box under the label Add a new fact and type a fact, for example I prefer Python over JavaScript for data work.
Click Add.
Compare: the new fact should appear in the list, and a new chat should be able to use it.
S39.10.where: Settings > Personalization > Memory > Manage memories > Add a new fact

S39.11.needs: a signed-in account with Persistent memory on
S39.11.note: The phrase is taken from the support document. No confirmation text for the saved fact was found in the code, so the tester should record what the reply shows.
steps: Open a new chat.
Type Remember that I prefer short answers and send.
Look at the reply for a note that the fact was saved.
Open Settings > Personalization > Memory > Manage memories and check the new fact is listed.
S39.11.where: Any chat > composer > type Remember that ... and send

S39.12.needs: a signed-in account, Persistent memory on
S39.12.note: The switch is disabled while Persistent memory is off.
steps: Open Settings, Personalization, and make sure Persistent memory is on.
Turn on Save memories from chats.
Chat for a few turns and state a lasting detail, for example I work as a nurse in Denver.
Open Manage memories and compare: the new durable fact should appear without you asking.
S39.12.where: Settings > Personalization > Save memories from chats (switch)

S39.13.needs: a signed-in account with a saved memory
S39.13.note: The text itself is the edit control; its screen reader label is Edit memory.
steps: Open Settings, Personalization, then click Manage memories.
Click the text of a saved memory to edit it.
Change the text, then click Save.
Compare: the new text should show in the list, and later chats should use the corrected text.
S39.13.where: Settings > Personalization > Memory > Manage memories > click a memory's text

S39.14.needs: a signed-in account with at least two saved memories
S39.14.note: The trash icon has no visible text; find it by its position at the end of each memory row.
steps: Open Settings, Personalization, then click Manage memories.
On one memory, click the trash icon labelled Delete memory fact.
In the dialog titled Delete this memory?, click Delete memory.
Compare: that one memory should leave the list and the others should stay.
S39.14.where: Settings > Personalization > Memory > Manage memories > Delete memory fact (icon)

S39.15.needs: a signed-in account with saved memories
S39.15.note: The button is disabled when no memories are saved.
steps: Open Settings and choose Personalization.
In the Memory block click Clear all memories.
In the dialog titled Delete all memory facts?, read the warning, then click Forget everything.
Compare: the count line should show no saved memories and the Manage memories list should be empty.
S39.15.where: Settings > Personalization > Memory > Clear all memories

S39.16.needs: a signed-in account with saved memories
S39.16.note: Some memory sources cannot be pinned and show Pinning is not available for this memory source.
steps: Open Settings, Personalization, then click Manage memories.
On one memory, click the pin icon labelled Pin memory.
Compare: the icon should change to Unpin memory and the memory should be shown as pinned.
Check that a pinned memory is kept when another memory is replaced (see Settings > Personalization > Memory > When memories disagree).
S39.16.where: Settings > Personalization > Memory > Manage memories > Pin memory (icon)

S39.17.needs: a signed-in account with memories from different sources (typed, imported, learned)
steps: Open Settings, Personalization, then click Manage memories.
Read the small grey line under each memory.
Compare: it should say Added by you, Imported, or Learned from a chat with the chat title as a link.
S39.17.where: Settings > Personalization > Memory > Manage memories (line under each memory)

S39.18.needs: a signed-in account with a saved memory
steps: Open Settings, Personalization, then click Manage memories.
Read the grey line under a memory.
Edit that memory, then read the line again.
Compare: the Updated date should show the date of the change.
S39.18.where: Settings > Personalization > Memory > Manage memories (grey line under each memory)

S39.19.needs: a signed-in account with Persistent memory on
S39.19.note: The rule is applied by the server, so there is no button for it. The Replaced line may take a page reload to appear.
steps: Save a memory by typing I live in Austin in Manage memories > Add a new fact.
In a new chat say I moved to Denver and send.
Open Settings > Personalization > Memory > When memories disagree and look for a line Replaced: I live in Austin.
Compare: in a later chat asking where you live, the reply should use Denver and not Austin.
S39.19.where: No control. The effect shows in Settings > Personalization > Memory > When memories disagree (Replaced: list).

S39.20.needs: a signed-in account with two memories that disagree
S39.20.note: The section shows No memory has replaced another. until a conflict exists, so the tester needs to create one first.
steps: Open Settings, Personalization, and scroll down to the Memory block.
Find the section titled When memories disagree.
Read the rule line: Pinned wins, then ones you added, then the newest.
If a Replaced line is listed, click Use the replaced one instead and compare which memory the assistant uses next.
S39.20.where: Settings > Personalization > Memory > When memories disagree (below the memory list)

labels.text: Import memory from other AI providers

S39.21.needs: a text or export file of memories from another assistant
steps: Open Settings, Personalization, and scroll to the row Import memory from other AI providers.
Click Start import.
In the dialog, choose Paste memories or Upload file, add the text or a file, then click Preview.
Tick the memories you want, click Import N selected, and compare: the memories should appear in Manage memories and later chats should use them.
S39.21.where: Settings > Personalization > Memory > Import memory from other AI providers > Start import

S39.22.needs: a signed-in account with saved memories
S39.22.note: The button is disabled when no memories are saved. The file format was not checked in the code.
steps: Open Settings, Personalization, and find the Memory block.
Click Export memories.
Open the downloaded file in a text editor or Preview.
Compare: it should list the saved memories in readable form.

labels.text: Use memories from outside this project

S39.24.note: The exact menu item that opens Project settings from a project page was not fully traced; the sidebar label was found.
steps: Open a project you own from Projects in the sidebar.
Open Project settings from the project's menu.
In the Memory section, read Use memories from outside this project and untick it to make project memory project-only.
Add a memory with Add a memory only this project uses, then open a chat in that project and a chat outside it and compare.
S39.24.where: Sidebar > Projects > open a project > Project settings > Memory

S39.26.needs: a workspace the account belongs to, with a second personal chat
S39.26.note: The workspace memory switch is in the Workspace console and needs an owner or admin; that part was not tested by reading only.
steps: Open Settings, Personalization, and find the block titled Where a memory applies.
Read the three rows: Account, Workspace, Project.
Open a workspace chat and a personal chat, ask what you know about the user, and compare that work memories do not appear in personal chats.
S39.26.where: Settings > Personalization > Memory > Where a memory applies (Account, Workspace, Project); workspace on/off is in Workspace > Policy > Memory

labels.text: This answer came from your saved memories, not the web.

S39.27.needs: a signed-in account with saved memories
S39.27.note: The note is shown for one search-notice state; when it appears in an ordinary reply was not confirmed. The Research panel memory list only shows in research runs.
steps: Save a memory, such as I work as a nurse, then open a new chat.
Ask a question that depends on it, such as what do you know about my job.
Read the note under the reply for This answer came from your saved memories, not the web.
Compare: the note should appear only when memory shaped the reply.
S39.27.where: Chat > a reply that used saved memory: the note under the reply, or the Memory section in the Research panel

labels.text: Temporary chats never read or save memory.

S39.28.needs: a signed-in account with saved memories
S39.28.note: The exclusion itself is applied by the server; the composer plus menu row label was taken from the shared constant.
steps: Start a temporary chat with File > New Temporary Chat, or from the composer choose Temporary chat.
Read the composer note: Temporary chats never read or save memory.
Ask what you know about me, and compare: no saved memories should be used.
Afterward open Settings > Personalization > Memory > Manage memories and check that nothing from the temporary chat was added.
S39.28.where: File > New Temporary Chat (desktop), or the composer's plus menu > Temporary chat

S39.29.note: Credentials and other sensitive facts are refused by the server automatically and have no control.
steps: Open Settings, Personalization, and find the block titled Never remember.
Type a term such as my home address in the box labelled Term to never remember and click Add.
Ask the assistant in a new chat to remember a term that matches, then check Manage memories.
Compare: the term should not be saved. Also check the switch Include sensitive topics in memory is off by default.
S39.29.where: Settings > Personalization > Memory > Never remember (and the switch Include sensitive topics in memory)

labels.text: Delete all chats in this workspace

S39.30.needs: a signed-in account with saved memories and chats
S39.30.note: The chat deletion control found is workspace-only; no personal delete-all-chats label was found in the files searched.
steps: Open Settings, Personalization, and click Clear all memories, then Forget everything. Check that the chats list is unchanged.
Open Settings > Privacy and find Delete all chats in this workspace, but do not confirm it unless you mean to.
Compare: deleting chats should not clear the memory list, and clearing memory should not delete chats.
S39.30.where: Settings > Personalization > Memory > Clear all memories (memory only). Chat deletion is in Settings > Privacy > Delete all chats in this workspace.

labels.text: Synced to your account, available on every device you sign into.
Read in every personal chat on every device, unless a project claims it.

S39.31.needs: a Free account or a paid account, with at least one saved memory, and two models available in the picker
S39.31.note: No control exists for this; the effect is applied in the server and client context code (apps/web/lib/services/turn-context-service.ts, apps/web/features/chat/lib/local-personal-context.ts, apps/web/lib/hooks/useChatStream.ts), which attaches the same personal context block to every model request. The visible label for the answer-level indicator is in apps/web/features/chat/components/messages/MessageBubble.tsx: 'Answered without your instructions and memory: they could not be loaded onto this device.' This appears only when the context could not be loaded in local mode. I did not verify the rendered result per model.
steps: Open a chat, pick one model from the model picker, and ask "What do you know about me?" or ask for a reply that uses a saved memory.
Switch to a different model in the same chat or a new chat and repeat the same question.
Compare the two replies: the saved memory and personalization should be used the same way with either model.

labels.text: Synced to your account, available on every device you sign into.

S39.32.needs: a second client signed in to the same account (for example a second browser or the phone app); a single account is enough
S39.32.note: Cross-client sync is in the memory store (packages/ui/unified-chat/src/stores/memoryStore.ts), which saves to the server through apps/web/app/api/memory/route.ts; the visible sync status text is shown only when the store is in the 'synced' state, and the 'Settings' item is in the account menu (apps/web/shared/components/layout/AccountMenuItems.tsx). I could not find a separate control for this, so the path to Memory is through Settings > Personalization. I did not verify the cross-device behaviour at runtime.
steps: On a computer, sign in to the same account and add a memory in Settings > Personalization > Memory (the Memory section under Personalization).
On a phone or a second browser, sign in to the same account and open Settings > Personalization > Memory.
Check that the memory added on the first client is listed on the second client, and that a new chat on the second client uses it.
Look for the line 'Synced to your account, available on every device you sign into.' under the memory list on the first client.
